Actualmente impulsamos Artemis, un software innovador de monitoreo inteligente de la salud diseñado para optimizar el seguimiento clínico y preventivo mediante herramientas digitales eficientes y seguras.
summary:
ARTEMIS HEALTH is a web-based prototype designed to support astronauts' well-being through the monitoring and visualization of four key indicators: resting heart rate, sleep duration, fatigue, and perceived stress.

We developed a platform that allows users to record observations, explore historical data, visualize trends, and compare new measurements with their personal history. It also incorporates simulated data and datasets from space research and ground-based analog studies, clearly identifying their sources and limitations.

Our solution addresses the challenge by transforming health-related information into organized, accessible, and understandable visual insights. We use React, Vite, TypeScript, Python, FastAPI, Supabase, and Recharts, with deployment through Vercel. ChatGPT supports project planning and documentation, while OpenAI Codex assists with coding and implementation.

This project is important because monitoring changes in astronauts' well-being is relevant to the challenges of human space exploration. ARTEMIS HEALTH demonstrates how technology and data visualization can support better understanding of individual trends, promoting informed awareness without replacing medical professionals or providing clinical diagnoses.
details:
ARTEMIS HEALTH is a web-based platform designed to support the monitoring and understanding of astronauts' well-being during space exploration. It allows users to record four key indicators: resting heart rate, sleep duration, fatigue, and perceived stress. The information is stored and organized in an interactive dashboard where users can explore historical records, visualize trends, and compare new observations with their personal history through descriptive statistics.

The platform also provides educational information and incorporates datasets related to space research and ground-based analog studies. It distinguishes simulated, manually reported, and publicly available data to ensure transparency and preserve the context of each observation.

ARTEMIS HEALTH offers several benefits: it centralizes relevant information, makes changes easier to understand through visualizations, encourages awareness of individual well-being patterns, and provides an accessible way to explore space-related research. Its intended impact is to demonstrate how digital tools and data analysis can support astronauts' well-being and contribute to future human space exploration.

We developed the project using React, Vite, and TypeScript for the frontend, Python and FastAPI for the backend, Supabase for database management, and Recharts for data visualization. The application is intended to be deployed through Vercel.

Artificial intelligence played an important role in our development process. We used ChatGPT (GPT) to refine and strengthen our original idea, define the project's scope, organize functional and non-functional requirements, and improve technical documentation. We also leveraged Google Gemini and Anthropic Claude to assist with frontend and backend development, including code generation, implementation support, debugging, and technical problem-solving. Additionally, OpenAI Codex supported coding and software implementation. These AI tools helped our team accelerate development, explore technical solutions, and improve the overall quality of the prototype.

The creative aspect of ARTEMIS HEALTH lies in combining personal tracking, historical comparisons, educational content, and space-related datasets in one platform. Our team considered data reliability, privacy, accessibility, scientific transparency, technical feasibility, and the limitations of simulated and research data.

Importantly, ARTEMIS HEALTH does not diagnose diseases, predict medical conditions, or replace professional healthcare. Its purpose is to provide clear, responsible, and understandable information that could contribute to the future of astronaut health monitoring.
